title: PRIVACY HAS AN EXIT PROBLEM
subtitle: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN PRIVATE MONEY TOUCHES A PUBLIC WORLD.

blocks.text: STRONG CRYPTOGRAPHY CAN PROTECT A PAYMENT. IT CANNOT CONTROL EVERYTHING THAT HAPPENS BEFORE OR AFTER IT.
THE PRIVACY BOUNDARY MATTERS.

A fully shielded Zcash transfer can keep protected sender information, recipient information and the transferred amount from being exposed as ordinary public blockchain data. That is a powerful property. It is not a promise that every surrounding interaction becomes private.

People still acquire coins, use wallets, connect to networks, interact with exchanges, pay merchants and sometimes move value between transparent and shielded environments. Each boundary deserves its own threat model.
01 // TRANSPARENT TO SHIELDED

When value crosses between transparent and shielded parts of Zcash, the transparent side remains visible. Shielding protects what happens inside the shielded system, but it does not rewrite the public history that existed before the funds entered it.

Users should also avoid assuming that simply passing a distinctive amount through a privacy system automatically destroys every possible correlation. Zcash privacy guidance specifically warns about metadata and transaction linkability.
02 // SHIELDED TO TRANSPARENT

Deshielding creates another boundary. Information associated with the transparent destination is public. If surrounding behavior makes an exit unusually recognizable, outside observers may gain clues even though the internal shielded payment graph itself remains protected.
THE SHIELDED GRAPH CAN BE PRIVATE WHILE YOUR BEHAVIOR AROUND ITS EDGES STILL TALKS.
03 // EXCHANGES KNOW WHAT YOU TELL THEM

Cryptographic privacy on a blockchain does not erase records held by a custodial exchange or another service. If a service knows your account identity, deposit or withdrawal details, that information exists outside the shielded protocol's confidentiality guarantee.
04 // THE NETWORK IS ANOTHER LAYER

Zcash documentation notes that peer-to-peer networking can expose IP-level information to network observers and warns that network data can potentially be correlated with transactions. Protecting payment contents and protecting network origin are different problems.
05 // YOU CAN DISCLOSE YOUR OWN PRIVACY

Transaction IDs, amounts, counterparties, screenshots, addresses and viewing information can all create linkages when shared. Zcash supports selective disclosure precisely because private payment information sometimes needs to be revealed intentionally to an auditor or another trusted party.
That is a feature, not a contradiction. Privacy means controlling disclosure. But control only works when the user understands what is being disclosed and to whom.
WHAT SHIELDED ZCASH ACTUALLY PROMISES

The useful claim is narrower and stronger than 'invisible money.' Shielded Zcash allows consensus to validate transactions without publishing protected payment details in the ordinary transparent form. The transaction still exists. Fees, timing and other protocol or network metadata can remain observable, while information outside the protocol can still identify a user.
PRIVACY IS NOT A SWITCH. IT IS A BOUNDARY YOU HAVE TO UNDERSTAND.
WHY THIS MAKES SHIELDED PRIVACY MORE INTERESTING — NOT LESS

Good privacy engineering does not require pretending that every layer is solved. It separates what is protected from what is exposed. Zcash's shielded protocol addresses a fundamental layer: it makes public disclosure of sender, recipient and amount unnecessary for fully shielded payment verification.
Everything outside that boundary still deserves careful handling. The cryptography can protect the transaction. Operational privacy protects the context.
THE DIFFERENCE IN ONE LINE.
THE CRYPTOGRAPHY CAN PROTECT THE TRANSACTION. IT CANNOT PROTECT INFORMATION YOU REVEAL SOMEWHERE ELSE.
